quote: But the basic problem is that even if the monetary authority knew the "natural" rate, and attempted to peg the market rate at that level, it would not be led to a determinate policy.
note: the basic problem: even knowing the natural rate, pegging the market rate at it gives no determinate policy

quote: The "market"rate will vary from the natural rate for all sorts of reasons other than monetary policy.
note: the market rate departs from the natural rate for reasons other than monetary policy

quote: The actual course of monetary growth will be analogous to a random walk, buffeted this way and that by the forces that produce temporary departures of the market rate from the natural rate.
note: monetary growth would follow something like a random walk

quote: I often studied an unidentified spending shock in the private sector that operated to increase the velocity of money and, if the central bank was slow to respond, would drive both the price level and money-wage level toward correspondingly higher paths
note: the velocity shock: an unidentified private spending shock driving prices and money wages to higher paths

quote: I supposed that this velocity shock would be neutral for quantities and relative prices if and when firms and workers formed correct expectations of the money-wage and price responses to the upward shift in the demand price.
note: neutral for quantities and relative prices once expectations are correct (his note 12: for every equilibrium path)

quote: Yet firms and workers have no way of perceiving such neutrality at the start.
note: no way of perceiving the neutrality at the start

quote: simulationreduces the inflation rate not only through the traditional channelof lower output, but also by causing a reductionin the relative price of importsand in the relative price of food and energy, as well as an appreciationin the effective exchange rate.
note: the three channels of international feedback: lower relative import prices, lower relative food and energy prices, an appreciation

quote: But Fellnerarguedthat holdingthe presentinflationrateis notfeasiblebecauseit is not a credible policy.
note: Fellner: holding the present inflation rate is not a credible policy

quote: If attempted, economic agents will believe that any higher inflationratewill be accommodated.
note: Fellner: agents would expect any higher inflation to be accommodated

quote: Fellnerconcludedthatany credible policy must involve a commitmentto reducethe rateof inflation.
note: Fellner: a credible policy must commit to reducing inflation

quote: Gordon responded that stabilizinginflationat its current level was a feasible policy as long as authorities made clear their determinationnot to tolerateany furtherincreasesin the rateof inflation, includingincreases caused by randomshocks.
note: Gordon: stabilizing inflation is feasible if the authorities make clear they will tolerate no further increase
